explanation: With referential integrity, a foreign key must match an existing referenced key value, or be null only when null is allowed. Here the stem states that Orders.CustomerID is NOT NULL, so NULL is not valid. Among the choices, 12 is the only value that appears in Customers, so it is the only value that satisfies referential integrity.
prompt: An Orders table has a CustomerID foreign key that references Customers.CustomerID. Assume Orders.CustomerID is NOT NULL. Customers currently contains CustomerID values 10, 12, and 15. Which Orders value satisfies referential integrity?
reviewConcept: A foreign key must match an existing parent key, unless null is permitted for an optional relationship.

source.title: The Relational Model and Relational Algebra
